name: scan_directory
description:
Scan a folder of photos into the imagic library.

        Use this first, before any culling, editing, or exporting: nothing
        else works on photos that have not been ingested. Give an absolute
        path to a folder of RAW or JPEG/PNG/TIFF files. Subfolders are
        included. Re-scanning is safe; already-known files are skipped.

        Pass the path exactly as the user gave it, whole and unedited.
        Folder names often contain spaces and " - " (for example
        "Holland 2025 - people-free"); never split or shorten a path at a
        dash. Everything inside the folder is imported, so if the folder
        does not exist the tool errors with the nearest matches, and if a
        similarly named folder sits beside it (or inside it) the tool
        refuses and lists them: ask the user which one they mean. Set
        confirm_exact_path=true only when the user has confirmed that exact
        folder is the one they want.
        Returns counts of discovered, newly ingested, and skipped files.

        On a remote connection this can take minutes on a big card: past a
        short budget it returns {"status": "running", "job_id": ...}
        instead — call get_job_status with that job_id to keep checking and
        get the same result shown above once it is ready. Local clients
        always get the result directly.

name: analyze_photos
description:
Run AI quality scoring and auto-culling on all pending photos.

        Scores sharpness, exposure, and composition, detects duplicates, and
        sorts photos into keep, trash, or culled (undecided). Optional
        thresholds are 0.0 to 1.0: a photo scoring at or above keep_threshold
        becomes keep, at or below trash_threshold becomes trash. Leave both
        unset to use the user's configured defaults. Can take a while on a
        large library; heavier AI models are skipped automatically when not
        installed. Returns analysis stats plus per-status library counts.

        Only pending photos are scored: already-analysed photos keep their
        stored score, even if the scorer has improved since. Use
        reanalyze_stale_photos for those.

        smart_rank (default false, experimental) adds a second pass after
        the fast cull: an image-understanding model rates which analysed
        photos are worth keeping and which are snapshots (signs, parked
        cars, floors), and the whole library is re-ranked from that. It
        also re-ranks photos analysed earlier, so it can be used on its own
        with no pending photos. Opt in only when the user wants better top
        picks over speed: it needs a one-time download of about 600 MB if
        this machine has never used photo search, and adds roughly two
        minutes per 1,000 photos. It never re-runs the analysis, never
        changes a manual keep/trash decision, and if it fails or is
        unavailable the fast cull's results stay as they were. The reply
        carries a smart_rank block with the estimate, status and counts.

        Remote: dispatched as a background job past the call budget, like
        scan_directory — poll get_job_status with the returned job_id.

name: reselect_photos
description:
Instantly re-rank analysed photos from their stored scores.

        Use this instead of analyze_photos when photos are already scored
        and you only want a different selection: it re-applies thresholds
        and the keep-limit from stored data in well under a second, with no
        re-analysis. Manual picks (statuses the user or set_photo_status
        chose) are always preserved and reported as manual_preserved.

        mode="pipeline" (default) reruns the normal decision engine:
        keep/trash thresholds plus the shoot-relative selection pass, with
        target_count as a ceiling on keepers. That pass caps near-duplicate
        frames at 4 per look, so it can keep fewer than target_count; the
        result carries a note when that happens.

        mode="top_n" is what "give me the best N for a portfolio" means:
        exactly target_count photos become keep and every other analysed
        photo becomes culled (review), nothing ever moves to trash, and at
        most max_per_group of them (default 1) come from the same
        near-duplicate/burst group — the same grouping the app's own cull
        uses — so a shutter-happy burst cannot fill the selection with
        near-identical frames. If the one-per-group pool is smaller than
        target_count, the remainder is filled from the next-best frames
        regardless of group, and the result says so. target_count is
        required.

        Great for live tweaking: call it repeatedly with different values
        until the user likes the counts. Returns keep/review/trash counts,
        manual_preserved, total_considered, and per-status library counts.
        A stale_scores block appears when some of the stored scores came from
        an older scorer; re-ranking cannot fix those, so relay it and offer
        reanalyze_stale_photos rather than re-cutting again.

name: check_score_freshness
description:
Check whether stored quality scores came from the current AI scorer.

        Scores are saved once and never recomputed, so photos analysed before
        a scorer improvement keep the verdict the old code gave them. This
        reports how many scored photos are stale, which scorer versions they
        carry, how many can be re-scored automatically, and how many are the
        user's own manual decisions and so are left alone. Cheap: one small
        set of counts, no analysis. Call it when a score looks wrong for the
        photo, when the user questions a verdict, or before trusting stored
        scores for a selection. The advice field says what to do next.

name: reanalyze_stale_photos
description:
Re-score photos whose stored scores came from an older AI scorer.

        The fix for what check_score_freshness reports: hands every stale
        photo the pipeline owns back to the analyser and runs a full analysis
        pass on them, so their scores and cull reasons reflect the current
        scoring rules. reselect_photos cannot do this: it re-ranks stored
        numbers. The user's manual keep/trash decisions are never re-scored
        and come back as manual_skipped. Takes as long as analyze_photos does
        for that many photos, so tell the user before starting on a large
        library. Returns analysis stats plus per-status library counts.

        Remote: dispatched as a background job past the call budget, like
        scan_directory — poll get_job_status with the returned job_id.

name: get_library_stats
description:
Get photo counts per pipeline status (pending, keep, trash, ...).

        Cheap. Call it to orient yourself before deciding what to do next,
        or to report progress to the user after a scan, analysis, or export.

name: list_photos
description:
List photos with id, filename, path, status, score, description and capture time.

        name finds photos by file name, the way people refer to them
        ("DSC04851"): case-insensitive, matches part of the name, and takes
        several comma-separated names at once. Use it to turn the names a
        user mentions into the photo ids every other tool expects.

        taken is when the photo was shot (ISO time from EXIF): the way to
        group a shoot by day or by evening ("the sunset frames") when there
        is no description. taken_after / taken_before filter by it (ISO,
        inclusive; a bare date covers the whole day), for example
        status="keep", taken_after="2026-09-22T18:00": on a big shoot,
        filter rather than listing everything. Capture times are read by
        analyze_photos, so run it before filtering by time; until then the
        response's note says how many photos have no time yet. Filter by status (pending, keep, trash, culled, exported, error) or
        omit it for everything. Use limit and offset to page through large
        libraries; the response includes the total match count. Photo ids
        from this list are what every per-photo tool expects.

name: get_photo
description:
Get full details for one photo: status, scores, EXIF, edit state.

        Use it when you need more than the list row, for example the AI
        caption, cull reasons, camera settings, or whether it has edits.

name: set_photo_status
description:
Override a photo's cull decision: pending, keep, trash, or culled.

        Use this to act on the user's verdicts ("keep number 12, trash 15")
        or to promote undecided (culled) photos after reviewing them.
        Trash never deletes files; it only excludes photos from export.

name: list_presets
description:
List available looks: the user's saved presets, scene presets, color grades and experimental presets.

        my_presets are the looks the photographer saved in the imagic editor
        ("Save current as preset"), by name, with the sliders each one moves.
        When the user mentions "my preset" or a look by a name that is not a
        built-in key, it is one of these.

        Scene presets (for example portrait, low_light) add slider offsets
        tuned for a shooting situation. Color grades (for example film_warm,
        moody, bw_classic) set an overall artistic look. Experimental presets
        (for example bleach_bypass, cinestill, infrared_bw) are one-click
        finishing effects from the editor's EXPERIMENTAL section, layered over
        everything else. Show these to the user when they ask what styles or
        filters are available, then use apply_preset.

name: apply_preset
description:
Apply a saved preset, scene preset, color grade or experimental preset to the given photos.

        preset_name must be a key from list_presets, or the name of one of
        the user's my_presets (case does not matter). A saved preset sets
        every slider it holds, like loading it in the editor; the photo's own
        crop and mask layers stay. The look is stored the
        same way the desktop editor stores edits, so exports render exactly
        what the editor would show. Applying a second preset merges scene
        preset offsets and replaces the color grade; an experimental preset
        replaces the previous experimental preset and keeps the grade. A key
        listed both as a color grade and as an experimental preset
        (bleach_bypass) applies the experimental preset; for the grade, use
        apply_adjustments {"color_grade": "bleach_bypass"}.

name: list_luts
description:
List the colour LUTs in the user's imagic library.

        The photographer adds LUTs they own (.cube, .3dl or Hald CLUT PNG)
        in the imagic editor's LUTs section; each is listed here by name with
        its kind (3D or 1D), size and the input it expects (Standard sRGB /
        Rec.709, or a camera log space such as S-Log3). When the user asks
        for "my LUT", a LUT by name, or a look that matches one of these,
        use apply_lut. The list is empty until the user has added some.

name: apply_lut
description:
Put one of the user's LUTs (see list_luts) on the given photos.

        lut_name is a name or id from list_luts (case does not matter), or
        "none" to remove the LUT. strength is 0..100: 100 is the full LUT,
        50 blends it half-way with the photo without it. The LUT is a
        finishing look applied after the rest of the edit, stored in each
        photo's edit stack (so it survives reopening and is baked into
        exports) and leaves every other adjustment as it was. Photos with a
        LUT export through the editor's engine, so the file matches what the
        editor shows.

name: apply_auto_color
description:
Auto Color: per-channel levels plus colour-cast removal, measured on each photo.

        The fix for faded or scanned prints and strong casts that Temperature,
        Tint, Blacks and Whites cannot reach: a print whose darkest pixel is a
        milky grey and whose cast differs between shadows and highlights.
        mode "color" sets each channel's own black and white point and snaps
        neutral midtones to grey (removes the cast); mode "contrast" uses one
        shared black and white point (restores range and depth, keeps the
        photo's colour: right for a warm sunset, coloured stage light or a
        toned black-and-white print); mode "off" removes it. strength 0..100
        blends with the uncorrected photo. It is stored in the edit stack and
        runs before every slider, so apply_adjustments and mask_adjust keep
        working on top of the corrected photo. Set a crop first if the frame
        has a white border or scanner edge: the measurement uses the crop.
        The result reports the cast and black/white points it measured.

name: harmonize_series
description:
Match exposure and white balance between neighbouring photos (drone mosaics, timelapse, events).

        The fix for visible seams in an orthomosaic (Pix4D, Metashape,
        WebODM) when clouds or the sun changed the light between frames, for
        timelapse flicker, and for uneven exposure across an event set. Each
        photo keeps its own grade; harmonize adds small Exposure, Temperature
        and Tint offsets (ordinary sliders, so exports and the Lightroom XMP
        handoff carry them) so that overlapping or consecutive frames match.
        mode "auto" uses GPS neighbours when the photos carry GPS (footprint
        overlaps from DJI altitude, yaw and focal length when present) and
        capture order otherwise; "gps" or "sequence" force one; "off" removes
        a previous harmonize. strength 0..100 scales the offsets. smoothness
        0.1..10 (default 1): higher also evens out slow changes across the
        whole set, lower only removes frame-to-frame jumps. dry_run=true
        reports without writing. Re-running replaces, never stacks. Returns
        per-photo offsets plus seam scores before and after (RMS brightness
        and colour mismatch across overlaps, in stops; under about 0.05 is
        invisible). Big sets return {"status": "running", "job_id"}: poll
        get_job_status. Pair with preview_mosaic to look at the result.

name: preview_mosaic
description:
Write a PNG preview of a drone set laid out by GPS, before and/or after harmonize_series.

        Preview only: an approximate layout from GPS, not a georeferenced
        map or a stitch (say so if you show it to the user). Frames are placed
        at their GPS positions, sized from altitude and focal length (or the
        median spacing) and rotated by gimbal yaw, with feathered overlaps
        (blend "seamlines" cuts them like a stitcher instead, which shows
        seams as edges). show "before", "after" or "both" side by side;
        "after" is the applied harmonize, or a dry run when none is applied.
        max_size is the PNG's long edge in pixels. group picks a separate
        flight or area (0 = the largest). Returns the PNG path, a seam
        heatmap PNG path, and seam_score_before/after (mean per-pixel
        brightness disagreement between overlapping frames, in stops). Look
        at the PNG; if seams remain, re-run harmonize_series with a higher
        smoothness, or lower it if broad light changes were flattened.

name: apply_adjustments
description:
Set editor slider values on one photo, or the same values on several.

        Pass exactly one of photo_id (a single photo — returns
        {"photo_id", "adjustments"}) or photo_ids (a list — applies the
        same adjustments to each independently and returns
        {"results": [...], "applied", "failed"}, one entry per photo so a
        bad id in the list does not lose the rest of the batch).

        adjustments maps slider names to numbers, for example
        {"exposure": 20, "contrast": 10, "temperature": 5}. The sliders, all
        -100..100 with 0 meaning no change unless a range is given:
          light: exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks
          colour: temperature, tint, vibrance, saturation, and per colour
            hsl_hue_<c>, hsl_sat_<c>, hsl_lum_<c> for c in red, orange,
            yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple, magenta
          presence: texture, clarity, dehaze
          detail: sharp_amount (0..150), sharp_radius (10..200),
            nr_luminance (0..100), nr_color (0..100)
          split toning: split_shadow_hue, split_highlight_hue (0..360),
            split_shadow_sat, split_highlight_sat (0..100), split_balance
          effects: vignette_amount, vignette_midpoint (10..90),
            grain_amount (0..100, film grain)
          looks: color_grade (a grade key from list_presets),
            color_grade_intensity (0..100), fx_preset (an experimental preset
            key from list_presets, or "none"), fx_amount (0..100),
            auto_color (0..100, Auto Color strength; see apply_auto_color),
            auto_color_mode ("color" or "contrast"),
            lut_name (a LUT from list_luts, or "none"), lut_strength (0..100)
          tone_curve_<luminance|red|green|blue>: a list of [x, y] points in 0..1
          crop_x, crop_y, crop_w, crop_h (pixels)
        To crop by aspect ratio without pixel maths, use crop_photo; to
        change only part of the frame, use mask_adjust. Values are absolute
        slider positions, not deltas, and an analysed photo nobody has
        edited already sits at its scene preset's values: for a relative
        request ("a stop brighter" = exposure +50, "a bit warmer"), read the
        current value with get_photo_edits and add to it. Values are
        clamped to range and unknown names are rejected with the valid list.
        New values overwrite previous values per slider; other sliders keep
        their settings. The sliders run the Lightroom way: negative
        highlights recovers bright areas, exposure +50 is one stop. A photo
        edited on imagic's legacy engine is moved to the current one first,
        keeping its look, so these values mean the same on every photo.

name: mask_adjust
description:
AI-mask part of a photo and adjust only that part (local adjustments).

        target is "subject", "sky", "people" or "background": imagic finds it
        with the same AI Masking the desktop editor uses (a second or two per
        photo, on this machine). adjustments takes the same slider names as
        apply_adjustments, for example {"exposure": 15, "clarity": 10} on the
        subject and {"exposure": -20, "saturation": -15} on the background to
        separate the two. Frame-level keys (crop, rotation, fx_preset) are
        rejected; set those with apply_adjustments.

        mode "relative" (default) adds the values on top of the photo's
        current look, like a Lightroom mask. mode "isolated" renders the
        region from the original with only these values, so later global
        edits stop affecting it (the editor's layer default).

        Each layer is saved as an editor mask layer named after the target
        (or name): exports include it, and the photo reopens in the editor
        with the layer as its own tab. Calling again with the same target or
        name replaces that layer instead of stacking another; remove=true
        deletes it. Pass photo_id for one photo or photo_ids for several
        (each gets its own mask). Returns the mask's coverage (fraction of
        the frame) and the photo's layer list; get_photo_edits lists layers
        too. On a remote connection a long batch runs as a background job:
        poll get_job_status with the returned job_id.

name: crop_photo
description:
Crop photos to an aspect ratio; imagic does the pixel maths.

        aspect is a ratio such as "3:1" (panorama strip), "16:9", "4:5",
        "1:1", "9:16" (stories), "original", or "free" with box. The crop is
        the largest of that shape that fits the frame, scaled by size (1.0 =
        as big as possible, 0.5 = half as wide, a tighter crop) and centred
        at center_x / center_y, fractions of the frame (0 = left/top, 1 =
        right/bottom; it is nudged to stay inside). For a horizon or subject
        that is not centred, move center_y / center_x towards it, for
        example center_y=0.45 for a horizon just above the middle. box =
        [x0, y0, x1, y1] fractions sets the crop exactly (aspect "free").
        clear=true removes the crop. Saved as the editor's crop, so exports
        are cropped and the editor shows the same frame. Returns the crop
        box as fractions and the result size.

name: save_preset
description:
Save a photo's current look as a named preset the user can reuse.

        The same file the editor's "Save current as preset" writes: every
        slider, the grade and any experimental preset, but never the crop or
        mask layers (those belong to one photo). It then appears in
        list_presets under my_presets, in the editor's preset menu, and can
        be applied to other photos with apply_preset. Refuses to replace an
        existing preset unless overwrite is true.

name: export_photos
description:
Render and export photos with all their edits to a folder.

        By default exports every keep photo (including previously exported
        ones, re-rendered). Pass photo_ids to export a specific set instead,
        or status to export a different group. dest_dir is created if needed;
        inside it, files are grouped into a subfolder named after the source
        shoot folder, and the result lists the exact file paths written.
        Rendering is CPU-bound and can take seconds per RAW file; the result
        reports exported and failed counts with per-photo errors.

        Set lightroom=True when the user wants to carry on in Adobe
        Lightroom: each proprietary RAW (ARW, CR3, NEF and similar) also gets
        a Camera Raw .xmp sidecar, and the RAW plus its sidecar are copied
        next to the export, so importing that folder into Lightroom opens
        the RAW with the same slider values. The result lists the sidecars
        in lightroom_sidecars. DNG, TIFF and JPEG files get no sidecar.
        The sidecar also carries the keep/reject decision as a standard XMP
        star rating (keep 1, trash -1; none when imagic has no decision), so
        an unedited keeper gets a sidecar holding just that.
        Experimental effects, mask layers, LUTs, heal and clone,
        lens/perspective corrections and the expert RAW engine settings
        have no Lightroom equivalent: they
        stay in imagic's own render, and lightroom_not_carried names them per
        photo. Tell the user when it is not empty, so they don't expect
        Lightroom's version to match, and name only what it lists. Everything
        else carries over: white balance, exposure and the tone sliders,
        texture, clarity, dehaze, vibrance and saturation, HSL, colour grades
        and split toning, the tone curve, sharpening, noise reduction,
        vignette, grain, crop and straighten. If the user plans to finish in
        Lightroom, prefer those.

        On a remote connection dest_dir is restricted: a bare or relative
        name (e.g. "delivery") always resolves under the user's configured
        export folder, and an absolute path must be inside that folder or
        one listed in their imagic config's mcp.remote_allowed_folders —
        anything else comes back as an error explaining where exports go
        and how to allow another folder. It is also dispatched as a
        background job past the call budget, like scan_directory — poll
        get_job_status with the returned job_id. Local clients are
        unrestricted and always get the result directly.

name: get_photo_edits
description:
Read back a photo's current adjustments and edit state.

        Returns the slider values that are set, the active color grade and
        scene preset, saved snapshot names, and whether the photo was
        touched in the desktop editor. For a photo nobody has edited, the
        values are its scene preset's starting point (starting_point says
        so): the base any relative change ("brighter", "a stop up") adds to. Use it to inspect what the user did
        manually, or to verify your own apply_adjustments calls.

        When imagic's own AI edit (AI Auto-Enhance / AI Optimize All in the
        editor) set the sliders, ai_explanation says why, per adjustment
        group: each slider's value and the measurements that set it, the
        look and the light it was chosen for, and any exposure-balance mask
        with its reason. A slider changed since is marked. Quote it rather
        than guessing why a value is what it is.

name: start_style_calibration
description:
Begin teaching imagic the user's personal editing style.

        This selects up to 8 diverse photos from the library as calibration
        scenarios. Your job as the AI after calling it: (1) present each
        scenario brief to the user, (2) ask them to open those photos in the
        imagic editor and edit them to their personal taste, (3) wait until
        the user says they are done, then (4) call record_style_calibration
        with the returned session_id. Do not call record_style_calibration
        before the user confirms they finished editing. If the library is
        empty this returns an error telling you to ask the user for their
        photos folder and call scan_directory first.

        Remote: on a big library this is dispatched as a background job past
        the call budget, like scan_directory — poll get_job_status with the
        returned job_id.

name: record_style_calibration
description:
Record the user's calibration edits into their style profile.

        Call this after the user says they finished editing the calibration
        photos from start_style_calibration. Normally leave edits as None:
        the edits the user made are read from the imagic library
        automatically. Only pass edits explicitly (a list of
        {"photo_id": ..., "adjustments": {...}}) if you gathered them some
        other way. Returns how many were recorded and a profile summary.

name: learn_style_from_library
description:
Train the user's style profile from photos already edited in imagic.

        Instant and needs no calibration session: it reads the slider
        adjustments the user has already made in imagic and feeds them into
        the same style profile that calibration builds. By default it learns
        from every edited photo in the library, most recently edited first,
        up to limit; pass photo_ids to train on a specific set instead.
        Safe to re-run any time: each run refines the profile with the
        photos' current edits. Use it after start_style_calibration to
        deepen a fresh profile, or on its own to train from a back catalog
        of edited photos with no session at all. Returns learned and
        skipped counts, the scenarios covered, and a profile summary.

        Remote: dispatched as a background job past the call budget, like
        scan_directory — poll get_job_status with the returned job_id.

name: match_style_from_examples
description:
Copy the look of a few edited photos onto the rest of a shoot.

        The photographer edits a few photos from a shoot; call this to
        apply that same look to the rest of the shoot. Different from
        apply_my_style: this matches THESE examples, not the saved profile.
        By default every edited photo in scope is an example and every
        unedited photo in scope is a target; pass example_photo_ids or
        target_photo_ids to control either side, and directory to scope
        the match to one shoot folder. Needs at least 2 edited examples.
        The match is session local and never changes the saved style
        profile unless save_to_profile is true, which also feeds the
        examples into the profile. Returns example and target counts plus
        the scenarios the examples covered.

name: get_style_profile
description:
Get the user's learned style profile, if one exists.

        Use it to check whether calibration has been done and to describe
        the learned style back to the user. Returns profile: null with
        guidance when no calibration has been recorded yet.

name: apply_my_style
description:
Apply the user's learned personal style to the given photos.

        Looks up the style profile built by calibration, gets suggested
        slider adjustments (optionally for a named scenario such as the ones
        from start_style_calibration), and applies them to each photo so
        exports render in the user's taste. Errors with guidance if no
        profile exists yet.

name: get_preview_url
description:
Get the local live-preview URL showing your edits in real time.

        imagic runs a small local web page that shows, live, what you are
        doing to the user's photo library as you call these tools: scans,
        culls, edits, and exports appear there the moment they happen. It
        normally opens automatically in the user's browser when this MCP
        server starts. Call this if the user asks to see what you are
        doing, asks for a link, or says the preview window is not open:
        tell them the URL, or that it should already be open in their
        browser. running is false if the local preview server could not
        start this session (for example a locked-down sandbox); in that
        case just say so, it is nothing to fix on the user's end.

name: get_job_status
description:
Check on a long-running job started by another tool on a remote connection.

        scan_directory, analyze_photos, reanalyze_stale_photos,
        export_photos, and learn_style_from_library each dispatch as a
        background job on a remote connection when they cannot finish
        within that call's own budget, returning {"status": "running",
        "job_id": ...}. Call this with that job_id to keep checking: it
        waits up to wait_seconds (capped at 30) for the job to finish before
        answering, so a short loop of calls is enough to follow it to
        completion. Once finished it returns exactly what the original tool
        call would have returned. Only one long job runs at a time; while
        one is running, other tools answer {"status": "busy", ...} instead
        of their normal result. Local (stdio) clients can use this too, but
        their long tools always finish synchronously, so there is normally
        nothing to poll.
